newsitem.title: UK: ITV to offer full weekend Formula One coverage.
newsitem.headline: ITV to offer full weekend Formula One coverage.

text.p: ITV will offer viewers a regular four-programme weekend package when it begins coverage of Formula One motor racing in March.

The ITV coverage, which is being sponsored by Texaco Inc, will begin on Saturdays when live coverage of the qualifying session is featured in a 90-minute programme. A 15-minute race news update will follow on Saturday evening.
Race commentary on Sundays will be supplied by veteran Murray Walker and former Formula One driver Martin Brundle and there will be a one-hour highlights show on Sunday evenings.
"Formula One will bring a new audience to ITV," said ITV network director Marcus Plantin, adding that the coverage would be the centrepiece of ITV programming for 17 weekends.
ITV outbid the BBC to win the contract for Formula One. The network, in partnership with BSkyB, has also won the rights to English soccer's F.A. Cup from next season.
"It is extremely important to have the best sport on this channel," said Plantin, adding that ITV would continue to screen soccer's European Champions' League.
The Formula One coverage is the responsibility of production company MACh1, a consortium of Anglia Television, Meridian Broadcasting and Chrysalis Sport.

MACh1 executive producer Neil Duncanson said the ITV coverage would differ from that of the BBC in that it would be in stand-alone programmes rather than wrapped into sports shows like Grandstand. He also said it would be presented live from the location rather than anchored in a London studio.
There will be five two-minute commercial breaks during each race. Duncanson said any key action which had been missed would be replayed immediately after the breaks.
Texaco's Guy Vigar said the company was paying 3.4 million pounds to sponsor the coverage, rising to 3.8 million pounds in the third and final year of the agreement.
Texaco plan to complement its sponsorship with press and radio advertising, posters and forecourt promotions.
The Grand Prix season begins in Melbourne with the Australian Grand Prix on March 9. It ends on October 26 when Estoril hosts the Portuguese Grand Prix.
